description: Leaders love AI because it makes knowledge instantly reusable—drafts, code, analysis on demand. A recent study uses a formal model to show what happens when “good-enough” answers become essentially free. As reuse rises, so does productivity but independent exploration falls and innovation flattens. The underlying issue is absorptive capacity—the ability to evaluate, adapt, and improve ideas rather than simply copy them. When reuse requires effort, people learn. When it’s frictionless, fewer invest in discovering better approaches. The solution isn’t to slow AI adoption but to build calibrated friction into tools, workflows, and talent systems—requiring independent attempts, prompting original input, and assessing how people use AI, not just what they produce. AI can make organizations faster overnight. Leaders must ensure it doesn’t make them shallower over time.
title: Research: Using AI Can Stifle Innovation. But It Doesn’t Have To.
